basis: The foundation's own page says it was created in 1992 by the jewellers Robert Boghossian and his sons and that it bought, restored and runs the villa; its team page lists a board of directors.

The governance page says the foundation is registered in British Columbia as a non-profit charitable society with a volunteer board elected at its AGM, and the tours page says the foundation is sole owner of the property and responsible for its management.

The register entry for Moravská galerie lists the legal form as a state contributory organisation in the central government sector, the gallery's about page lists the villa among its six buildings, and an audit office release of 2009 names the Ministry of Culture as its founder and records the audit.

The 2024 annual report (PDF pages 86 and 91) calls the National Heritage Institute a state contributory organisation run by the Ministry of Culture and reports its freedom of information cases, the villa's own site says the institute administers the villa since 2009, and a 2021 audit office release covers its audit and public procurement act.

The register entry lists Brno City Museum as a contributory organisation in the local government sector, its 2025 report (cover and page 2) gives the same form, and the villa's site calls the villa a department of Brno City Museum.

The register entry lists the Museum of Decorative Arts as a state contributory organisation in the central government sector, an audit office release of 2009 names the Ministry of Culture as its founder and records the audit, and an August 2025 news article says the museum took the villa into its property.

The 2024 annual report of the Gallery of West Bohemia (PDF page 5) lists the Plzeň Region as founder and the form as a contributory organisation, and says the Klatovská 110 building (Semler Residence) is run by the gallery and owned by the region.

The register entry lists the Prague City Gallery as a contributory organisation in the local government sector, its 2024 annual report refers to its founder's contribution (read through a web.archive.org copy), and its site says the gallery manages the villa.

The museum's own page calls it a state-funded organisation established by the City of Prague, the register entry lists a contributory organisation in the local government sector, and the 2024 annual report covers the villas as part of the museum.
